title: Hormonal coordination in humans
source: Questions and terms copied unchanged from the site's bank, except where marked for AQA GCSE Biology (8461) (status of the source: authored-gated-unreviewed). Terms and clues: 4.5.3-c25 bank term, first sentence of the bank's definition; 4.5.3-c28 bank term, first sentence of the bank's definition; 4.5.3-c16 bank term, first sentence of the bank's definition; 4.5.3-c24 bank term, first sentence of the bank's definition. Questions: 4.5.3-q10, 4.5.3-q16, 4.5.3-q19, 4.5.3-q11, 4.5.3-q25, 4.5.3-q20, 4.5.3-q12, 4.5.3-q13, 4.5.3-q15, 4.5.3-q14, 4.5.3-q17, 4.5.3-q21, 4.5.3-q23, 4.5.3-q18, 4.5.3-q22.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: testosterone
items.clue: The main male reproductive hormone, produced by the testes; it stimulates sperm production.

items.label: progesterone
items.clue: A hormone involved in the menstrual cycle which, with oestrogen, is involved in maintaining the uterus lining.

items.label: urea
items.clue: A waste substance lost from the skin in sweat and removed, with excess water and ions, via the kidneys in the urine.

items.label: ovulation
items.clue: The release of an egg from the ovary; from puberty eggs begin to mature and one is released approximately every 28 days.

questions.stem: The body fluids around a person's cells become too dilute. What is the effect on the cells?

options.text: they gain water by osmosis and work as normal
they gain water by osmosis and work less well
they lose water by osmosis and stop working well
they lose water by osmosis and work as normal

questions.explanation: Water moves into the cells by osmosis from the more dilute body fluids, and if body cells gain too much water by osmosis they do not function efficiently.

questions.stem: What is the role of follicle stimulating hormone (FSH) in the menstrual cycle?

options.text: it causes a mature egg to be released
it keeps the lining of the uterus in place
it causes an egg to mature in the ovary
it is released from the ovary at puberty

questions.explanation: Follicle stimulating hormone (FSH) causes maturation of an egg in the ovary.

questions.stem: A woman wants a method of contraception that does not use hormones. Which method and reason are correct?

options.text: a condom, which releases a hormone slowly
a diaphragm, which stops sperm reaching eggs
the pill, which kills sperm before they arrive
an implant, which stops sperm reaching an egg

questions.explanation: Barrier methods such as condoms and diaphragms prevent the sperm reaching an egg, so they control fertility without using hormones.

questions.stem: Which statement about the loss of water and other substances from the body is correct?

options.text: water lost in sweat is controlled by hormones
sweat contains water but no ions or urea
water lost from the lungs is not controlled
water lost from the skin is closely controlled

questions.explanation: Water leaves the body via the lungs during exhalation, and there is no control over water, ion or urea loss by the lungs or skin.

questions.stem: Which statement about the main reproductive hormones is correct?

options.text: oestrogen is produced by the pituitary gland
testosterone is produced by the testes
oestrogen is produced by the thyroid gland
testosterone is produced by the pituitary

questions.explanation: Testosterone is the main male reproductive hormone produced by the testes, and it stimulates sperm production.

questions.stem: How do oral contraceptives that contain hormones prevent pregnancy?

options.text: they inhibit FSH production so no eggs mature
they kill or disable sperm before fertilisation
they stop an embryo implanting in the uterus
they form a barrier that stops sperm reaching eggs

questions.explanation: Oral contraceptives contain hormones to inhibit FSH production so that no eggs mature.

questions.stem: How do the kidneys produce urine and help to maintain the water balance of the body?

options.text: only waste substances are filtered out of the blood
glucose and all useful ions are lost in the urine
urea is reabsorbed and glucose is lost in the urine
the blood is filtered and useful substances reabsorbed

questions.explanation: The kidneys produce urine by filtration of the blood and selective reabsorption of useful substances such as glucose, some ions and water, and excess water, ions and urea are removed in the urine.

questions.stem: A table gives the concentration of two substances in the blood entering a kidney and in the urine leaving it, in grams per dm3. Glucose: 1.0 in the blood and 0.0 in the urine. Urea: 0.3 in the blood and 20.0 in the urine. What do these figures show?

options.text: glucose is not filtered, so none reaches the urine
glucose is reabsorbed, so it is absent from urine
glucose is removed with the urea and lost from blood
urea and glucose are both reabsorbed by the kidney

questions.explanation: The blood is filtered and glucose is a useful substance that is selectively reabsorbed, so its concentration in the urine falls to zero while urea becomes concentrated.

questions.stem: Which statement describes a basic principle of kidney dialysis?

options.text: glucose passes from the blood into the dialysis fluid
urea passes from the blood into the dialysis fluid
useful ions pass from the blood into the fluid
water and ions pass from the blood into the fluid

questions.explanation: Dialysis treats kidney failure by allowing urea to pass out of the blood into a dialysis fluid that contains no urea, while useful substances are not lost.

questions.stem: On a hot day a person sweats a great deal and drinks very little, so the blood becomes too concentrated. What is the effect of ADH on the kidney tubules?

options.text: they become less permeable, so water is reabsorbed
they become more permeable, so more urine is produced
they become more permeable, so more water is reabsorbed
they become less permeable, so more sweat is produced

questions.explanation: ADH is released by the pituitary gland when the blood is too concentrated and acts on the kidney tubules, making them more permeable so that more water is reabsorbed back into the blood.

questions.stem: Which interaction between hormones helps to control the menstrual cycle?

options.text: LH inhibits FSH and causes an egg to mature
FSH inhibits oestrogen and maintains the lining
progesterone stimulates FSH and LH release
oestrogen inhibits FSH and stimulates LH release

questions.explanation: Oestrogen produced in the ovary inhibits the production of FSH and stimulates the release of LH, which then stimulates the release of the egg.

questions.stem: A woman does not release eggs because her level of FSH is too low. Which treatment could allow her to become pregnant in the normal way?

options.text: a fertility drug that contains FSH and LH
a fertility drug that contains progesterone
IVF, in which eggs are fertilised in her body
a fertility drug that contains only LH

questions.explanation: Giving FSH and LH in a 'fertility drug' to a woman stimulates the maturation and release of eggs, and she may then become pregnant in the normal way.

questions.stem: A student is suddenly frightened by a loud noise. Which gland releases adrenaline, and what effect does it have?

options.text: the adrenal gland; it raises the heart rate
the pituitary gland; it raises the heart rate
the thyroid gland; it reduces the heart rate
the pituitary gland; it lowers the heart rate

questions.explanation: Adrenaline is produced by the adrenal glands in times of fear or stress; it increases the heart rate and boosts the delivery of oxygen and glucose to the brain and muscles.

questions.stem: A graph of hormone levels during the menstrual cycle shows the level of LH rising to a sharp peak on day 14. What is happening on day 14?

options.text: an egg is starting to mature in the ovary
an egg is being released from the ovary
the lining of the uterus is being maintained
the lining of the uterus is breaking down

questions.explanation: Luteinising hormone (LH) stimulates the release of the egg, so a sharp peak in LH on day 14 indicates ovulation.

questions.stem: Which statement about IVF treatment is correct?

options.text: eggs are fertilised by sperm in the laboratory
eggs are fertilised by the sperm inside the mother
most IVF treatments result in a successful birth
multiple births from IVF carry very little risk

questions.explanation: In IVF the eggs are collected from the mother and fertilised by sperm from the father in the laboratory; the embryos are inserted into the uterus as tiny balls of cells.
